title: 집 · 거주지
intro: OPIc 설문에서 거의 항상 출제되는 핵심 주제로, 집 묘사 → 집에서의 일상 → 집과 관련된 경험(고장·문제) → 예전 집과 비교 순서로 나옵니다. 모든 답변은 '회사에서 차로 20분 거리 분당 아파트 15층, 방 3개·거실·부엌·화분 있는 베란다, 가족 넷이 8년째 거주'라는 하나의 집으로 통일하세요. 비교 질문에는 어릴 적 대전에서 살던 집이나 결혼 전후 살던 서울의 작은 아파트를 쓰면 자기소개 내용과 그대로 이어집니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Okay, let me tell you about my place.' → 집 기본 정보(분당 아파트 15층, 방 3개, 가족 넷, 8년째) → 공간 묘사(거실 → 부엌 → 방 3개 → 베란다) → 좋아하는 공간과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
묘사는 현관에서 안쪽으로 공간 순서대로 이동하면 길을 잃지 않아요. 'When you walk in, ~' / 'Next to ~, there's ~'.
가족과 사는 설정을 살려 '아이들 방', '가족 영화의 밤을 하는 거실 소파', '금요일 재택근무 하는 작은방' 같은 디테일과 느낌을 붙이면 IH 이상이 됩니다.
비교 질문은 어릴 적 대전 집(마당 있는 오래된 2층 주택) vs 지금 집(높은 층 아파트, 편리함)으로 차이 2가지와 느낌을 말합니다.

expressions.en: Okay, let me tell you about my place.
expressions.ko: 네, 저희 집에 대해 말해 볼게요.
expressions.note: 시작 문장. my place = 우리 집 (구어체)

expressions.en: I live in an apartment in Bundang with my family.
expressions.ko: 저는 가족과 함께 분당의 아파트에 살아요.

expressions.en: It has three bedrooms, a living room, and a kitchen.
We've lived here for about eight years.
expressions.note: have lived ~ for + 기간 = ~ 동안 살아 왔다

expressions.en: There are some plants on the veranda.
My favorite spot is the sofa in the living room.
expressions.ko: 제가 제일 좋아하는 곳은 거실 소파예요.

expressions.en: When you walk in, the first thing you see is the living room.
expressions.ko: 들어가면 가장 먼저 보이는 게 거실이에요.

expressions.en: My kids each have their own room.
expressions.note: each have their own ~ = 각자 ~이 있다

expressions.en: The smallest room is my home office.
expressions.ko: 가장 작은 방은 제 재택근무 공간이에요.

expressions.en: It gets a lot of sunlight in the afternoon.
The best part is that it's only 20 minutes from my office.
expressions.ko: 제일 좋은 점은 회사에서 20분밖에 안 걸린다는 거예요.
expressions.note: The best part is that + 문장

expressions.en: It's not fancy, but it really feels like home.
expressions.ko: 화려하진 않지만 정말 우리 집 같은 느낌이에요.
expressions.note: feel like home = 편안한 내 집 같다

expressions.en: I'd never trade it for a bigger place downtown.
expressions.ko: 시내의 더 큰 집과도 절대 바꾸지 않을 거예요.
expressions.note: trade A for B = A를 B와 바꾸다

expressions.en: Yeah, that's pretty much my place.

questions.en: I'd like to know about where you live. Can you describe your home? What does it look like, and how many rooms does it have?
questions.ko: 당신이 사는 곳에 대해 알고 싶습니다. 집을 묘사해 줄 수 있나요? 어떻게 생겼고, 방은 몇 개인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Okay, let me tell you about my place.' → 아파트 15층·방 3개·가족 넷 → 거실 → 부엌 → 방(아이들 방, 작은방) → 베란다 → 좋아하는 곳 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
공간 순서대로 이동하며 'When you walk in, ~', 'Next to ~' 표현을 쓰세요.
'It's not fancy, but it's really comfortable.'처럼 느낌 한 줄을 꼭 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my place. I live in an apartment in Bundang with my family. We live on the 15th floor. It has three bedrooms, a living room, and a kitchen. The living room is big, and there's a large sofa and a TV. My kids each have their own room. There's also a veranda with some plants. My favorite place is the sofa in the living room. Yeah, that's pretty much my place.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about my place. I live with my family in an apartment in Bundang, about 20 minutes from my office. We're on the 15th floor, and we've lived here for about eight years. When you walk in, the first thing you see is the living room. There's a big gray sofa and a TV, and that's where we have our family movie night every Friday. The kitchen is right next to the living room, so it's easy to talk while someone is cooking. We have three bedrooms. My son and my daughter each have their own room, and the smallest room is my home office for Fridays. There's also a veranda with lots of plants. It's not fancy, but it's really comfortable. Yeah, that's pretty much my place.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about my place. I live with my family in an apartment in Bundang, just a 20-minute drive from my office. We moved here from a small apartment in Seoul about eight years ago, and after all these years, it really feels like home. We're on the 15th floor, so the view is pretty nice, especially at night. When you walk in, the first thing you notice is the living room. It's bright and open, and there's a big gray sofa facing the TV. That sofa is basically the heart of our home, because that's where the four of us have movie night every Friday. The kitchen is right next to it, so whoever is cooking can still join the conversation. We have three bedrooms. My son and my daughter each have their own room, and as you can imagine, my son's room is always a mess. The smallest room is my home office, where I work on Fridays. And then there's the veranda, which is full of plants that I water every weekend. It's not fancy, but honestly, I'd never trade it for a bigger place downtown. So yeah, that's pretty much my place.

questions.en: What do you usually do at home? Tell me about a typical day at your home from morning to night.
questions.ko: 집에서 보통 무엇을 하나요? 아침부터 밤까지 집에서의 평범한 하루를 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Sure, let me tell you what I usually do at home.' → 아침(아침 식사, 아이들 등교 준비) → 저녁(가족 저녁, 숙제 봐주기) → 밤(TV·책) → 주말이나 금요일 이야기 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
First, Then, After that 같은 연결어로 시간 순서를 분명히 하세요.
금요일 재택근무와 가족 영화의 밤을 넣으면 다른 주제(영화, 직장)와 스토리가 이어집니다.

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you what I usually do at home. In the morning, I have breakfast with my family. It's always busy because my kids get ready for school. In the evening, I come home at around seven thirty. We have dinner together. After that, I help my kids with their homework. Then, I watch TV or read a book on the sofa. On Fridays, I work from home. Yeah, that's what I usually do at home.
answers.IH: Sure, let me tell you what I usually do at home. On weekdays, mornings at my place are pretty busy. First, I make coffee and have a quick breakfast with my family. My kids are usually rushing to get ready for school, so it's a little noisy. In the evening, I get home at around seven thirty, and we all have dinner together at the kitchen table. After that, I check my kids' homework, especially my daughter's math. Then, I relax on the sofa and watch the news or read a book. On Fridays, I work from home in the small room, so I can have lunch at home, which is nice. And Friday night is our family movie night in the living room. Yeah, that's a typical day at my home.
answers.AL: Sure, let me tell you what a typical day at my home looks like. On weekdays, the morning is pure chaos. I get back from jogging at around seven, make myself a coffee, and try to have breakfast with my family while my kids are rushing around looking for their school bags and socks. Once everyone's out the door, I head to work too. In the evening, I usually get home at around seven thirty, and we have dinner together at the kitchen table. That's actually my favorite part of the day, because it's the only time all four of us sit down and talk about our day. After dinner, I help my kids with their homework. My son is in middle school, so his math is getting pretty tough, and sometimes I have to look things up myself. Once the kids are in bed, I finally get some quiet time on the sofa with a book or a drama. Fridays are a bit different, since I work from home in the small room, and at night, we have our family movie night with popcorn. So yeah, that's pretty much a typical day at my home.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem at your home, like something breaking? Tell me what happened and how you handled it.
questions.ko: 집에서 무언가 고장 나는 등의 문제를 겪은 적이 있나요? 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, a problem at home? Let me think.' → 언제·무슨 일(겨울밤 부엌 싱크대 아래 물이 샘) → 내가 한 일(물 잠그기, 관리사무소 연락) → 해결(다음 날 수리) → 배운 점 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
과거 시제로 일관되게 말하고, 'I remember one time when ~'으로 시작하면 자연스러워요.
'Luckily, ~', 'Since then, I always ~'로 결말과 교훈을 붙이면 IH 이상이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Last winter, there was a water leak in my kitchen. It was late at night, and the floor was all wet. Water was coming from a pipe under the sink. I turned off the water right away. Then, I called the management office. A repairman came the next morning and fixed the pipe. It took about an hour. Luckily, it wasn't a big problem. Yeah, that's what happened.
answers.IH: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. I remember one time when we had a water leak in the kitchen. It was a Sunday night last winter, and my daughter came to me and said the kitchen floor was wet. When I checked, water was dripping from a pipe under the sink. I didn't know what to do at first, so I turned off the main water valve and put towels and a bucket on the floor. Then, I called the management office of our apartment complex. They said a repairman could come the next morning, so I took the morning off. He changed the old pipe in about an hour. Luckily, the water didn't go down to the apartment below us. Since then, I always check under the sink once in a while. Yeah, that's my story.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Actually, I remember one time when we had a pretty stressful water leak. It was a freezing Sunday night last winter, and we were just about to go to bed when my daughter shouted from the kitchen that her socks were wet. I went in, and sure enough, there was water all over the floor. It was coming from an old pipe under the sink. For a second, I didn't know what to do, but then I remembered where the main water valve was and turned it off. My family grabbed every towel in the house, and my son even used his old bucket from the beach. It was kind of funny, looking back. Then, I called the management office, and they said a repairman could come the next morning. So, I sent a quick message to my team and took the morning off. The repairman replaced the pipe in about an hour, and luckily, the water hadn't leaked down to our neighbors downstairs. That was a huge relief. Since then, I always make sure to check under the sink every few months. So yeah, that's my home disaster story.

questions.en: How is the home you live in now different from the home you lived in when you were a child?
questions.ko: 지금 사는 집은 어렸을 때 살던 집과 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's an interesting question.' → 어릴 적 집(대전의 마당 있는 오래된 2층 주택) → 지금 집(분당 아파트 15층) → 차이 2가지(크기·편리함 / 이웃·바깥 놀이) → 느낌 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'I used to ~, but now I ~', 'Compared to ~, ~ is much ~' 비교 틀을 꼭 쓰세요.
장점만 말하지 말고 '그래도 그리운 점' 하나를 넣으면 답변이 깊어집니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's an interesting question. When I was a child, I lived in a house in Daejeon. It was an old two-story house with a small yard. Now I live in an apartment on the 15th floor in Bundang. My apartment is much newer and more convenient. But my childhood home had a yard, and I played there every day. I miss that yard sometimes. Yeah, that's the difference between my two homes.
answers.IH: Oh, that's an interesting question. When I was a child, I lived with my parents in an old two-story house in Daejeon. It had a small yard with a persimmon tree, and I used to play there with my neighbors' kids every day. Now I live in an apartment on the 15th floor in Bundang with my own family. The biggest difference is convenience. My apartment is newer, warmer in winter, and there's a supermarket and a subway station nearby. In my old house, it was really cold in winter, and we had to walk a long way to the market. But there's one thing I really miss about my old house. My kids don't have a yard, so they play on their phones more than outside. Yeah, that's how my home has changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's an interesting question, because my home now is completely different from the one I grew up in. When I was a kid, I lived with my parents in an old two-story house in Daejeon. It had a small yard with a big persimmon tree, and every fall, my dad and I would climb up and pick persimmons together. Honestly, those are some of my favorite memories. Now I live with my own family in an apartment on the 15th floor in Bundang. Compared to my childhood home, my apartment is much more convenient. It's warm in winter, everything works, and there's a big supermarket and a subway station just ten minutes away. Back then, our house was freezing in winter, and the bathroom was so old that we sometimes had no hot water. On the other hand, I do miss having a yard. My kids spend most of their free time indoors, and they don't really know our neighbors, while I grew up playing outside with everyone on my street. So my home is much more comfortable now, but my childhood home had something special that I still miss. So yeah, that's how my home has changed.

pronunciation.tip: '베란다'가 아니라 v 소리로 'v뤤더'. 둘째 음절에 강세
첫 음절 'bed'에 강세, d는 거의 들리지 않게 '베(드)룸'

patterns.en: I started living in this apartment about eight years ago.
patterns.ko: 저는 약 8년 전에 이 아파트에 살기 시작했어요.

patterns.en: When you walk in, the first thing you notice is the bright living room with a big gray sofa.
patterns.ko: 들어가면 가장 먼저 눈에 띄는 건 큰 회색 소파가 있는 밝은 거실이에요.

patterns.en: My favorite place to relax is the sofa in our living room.
patterns.ko: 제가 쉬기 가장 좋아하는 곳은 거실 소파예요.

patterns.en: First, I make coffee. Then, I have a quick breakfast with my family.
patterns.ko: 먼저 커피를 만들어요. 그다음 가족과 간단히 아침을 먹어요.

patterns.en: Spending time with my kids at dinner helps me forget about work.
patterns.ko: 저녁 식사 때 아이들과 시간을 보내면 일을 잊는 데 도움이 돼요.

patterns.en: I remember one time when a pipe under the kitchen sink started leaking on a winter night.
patterns.ko: 겨울밤에 부엌 싱크대 아래 배관에서 물이 새기 시작했던 때가 기억나요.

patterns.en: Since then, I always make sure to check under the sink every few months.
patterns.ko: 그 이후로 저는 몇 달마다 싱크대 아래를 꼭 확인해요.

patterns.en: Compared to my childhood home in Daejeon, my apartment now is much more convenient.
patterns.ko: 대전의 어릴 적 집에 비하면 지금 아파트가 훨씬 편리해요.
